About Us

Protecting Innovation
with Precision

InventraIP is a dedicated Intellectual Property Rights consultancy committed to providing comprehensive, precise, and strategic protection for intellectual assets across the globe.

Our Story

A Firm Built on Expertise and Integrity

Inventra is a dedicated Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) consultancy committed to providing comprehensive, precise, and strategic protection for intellectual assets. We support innovators, entrepreneurs, research institutions, and established organizations in strengthening their competitive advantage through well-structured IP solutions.

With a team of seasoned patent analysts, trademark specialists, technology experts, and industry-trained professionals, Inventra delivers high-quality services adhering to international IP standards.

Our approach is grounded in accuracy, confidentiality, and strategic insight, ensuring that every engagement reflects exceptional professional excellence.

Mission

To advance and safeguard innovation through meticulously crafted Intellectual Property solutions, grounded in analytical depth, strategic foresight, and uncompromising professionalism.

Vision

To be a distinguished and globally respected IPR consultancy recognized for thought leadership, ethical integrity, and excellence in shaping the future of intellectual property protection, management, and strategy.

Services / Novelty Search

Novelty Search

Novelty searches powered by technology and guidance to empower a competitive edge. The ideal time to conduct a patentability search is before preparing a patent application.

  • 📜
    Prior Art Search →
    Research identifying patent and non-patent prior art, presented in an easy-to-understand report — enabling informed decisions on invention direction.
  • 📑
    Patentability and Marketability Report →
    Comprehensive report on novelty vs. prior art, feature-by-feature comparison matrix, and identification of potential licensees, funding sources, and competitors.

  • ✓ Technical opinions to accelerate informed decision-making

Key Deliverables

  • Confirm novelty of the invention

  • Market insight report

Services / Litigation Support

Patent Litigation Support

Litigation search driven by unrivalled strategy, relevancy, and reporting accuracy. We take a systematic approach to analyzing all aspects of your business and providing timely counsel.

  • 🚫
    Invalidation / Validity / Opposition Search →
    Find patents and non-patent literature to challenge novelty and inventiveness of claims — helping defend against infringement suits and gaining freedom to operate.
  • 🕵️
    Infringement Analysis / Evidence of Use →
    Identify products, processes or services infringing on a patent; provide arguments for proving infringement or redesigning around existing IP.
  • 🟢
    Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) Search →
    Identify in-force and expired patents in subject matter of interest to ensure safe product launch and sustainable business strategy.

Key Deliverables

  • Search Report Summary
  • Summary of Search Results
  • Claims Mapping Chart
  • Search Strategies (Patent and Non-Patent)
  • References with highlighted excerpts

Services / Patent Drafting

Patent Drafting Services

We draft patent applications not only to meet patent office necessities, but to make them future-proof with the broadest possible coverage that cannot be circumvented by third parties.

  • 📝
    Patent Specification Drafting →
    Drafting utility patent specifications (provisional and non-provisional) and design patent specifications for USPTO, EPO, JPO, PCT, India, and more.
  • 🖊️
    Patent Illustrations →
    CAD-created patent drawings by highly competent experts across a variety of technical domains — precise, clear, and meeting the strictest guidelines.
  • 📬
    Office Action Response →
    Creating comprehensive responses to issued office actions with arguments and amendments that address examiner rejections in accordance with patent office regulations.

Key Deliverables

  • Claim Drafting
  • Patent Proofreading
  • Non-provisional specification
  • Provisional specification
  • Utility and Design Drawings
  • Trademark Illustrations
  • Non-final and Final office action responses

FAQs

Frequently Asked Questions

Clear answers to the most common intellectual property questions from inventors and businesses.

What is a patent and what does it protect?
+
A patent is a legal right granted by the government for an invention. It provides exclusivity for a limited period — typically 20 years from the filing date for utility patents. The owner has the right to exclude others from making, using, or selling the invention. Patents cover products, processes, machines, and compositions of matter. They encourage innovation and investment while requiring full public disclosure of the invention.
Can I obtain international patent protection?
+
There is no single patent that provides worldwide protection. Patent rights are territorial. However, inventors can use the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) to seek protection in over 150 countries through a single international filing. After the PCT phase, you must enter national or regional patent offices. Strategic country selection is critical to managing costs and maximizing protection.
How do I know if I need a patent, trademark, or copyright?
+
Patents protect functional inventions and technical solutions. Trademarks protect brand names, logos, and slogans. Copyrights protect creative expression such as text, software, music, and artwork. A single product may involve multiple IP rights — a device may be patented, branded with a trademark, and include copyrighted software. Consulting IP professionals helps clarify which strategy is right for your innovation.
I have an invention — how do I find if something similar already exists?
+
You can conduct a prior-art search using public patent databases including USPTO, WIPO Patentscope, and Google Patents. Non-patent literature such as academic papers should also be reviewed. InventraIP offers professional novelty searches that provide deeper legal analysis, assess patentability, and inform claim drafting and filing strategy.
What is a Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis?
+
An FTO analysis identifies in-force patents in subject matter of interest to a customer based on a product or hypothetical claim. It helps determine whether making, using, or selling a product infringes any existing patents. FTO searches allow businesses to avoid product redesign, prevent infringement damages, and identify possible licensing options before market entry.
What is the difference between TM and ®?
+
The TM symbol indicates a claim of trademark rights without registration and can be used for goods or services. The ® symbol may only be used after official registration with the relevant trademark office. Using ® without registration is illegal. TM provides limited common-law rights, while registration provides stronger legal protection and public notice.
Is a trademark search necessary before filing?
+
A trademark search is not legally required, but it is highly recommended. The search helps identify existing marks that may conflict with yours, reducing the risk of application refusal or legal disputes. Similarity in sound, appearance, or meaning can cause issues even without identical names. Professional searches are more comprehensive and support informed brand decisions.
How do I finance and market my invention?
+
Inventors can finance inventions through personal investment, licensing, or external funding. Common sources include angel investors, venture capital, and government grants (SBIR/STTR). Licensing allows inventors to earn royalties without manufacturing. Strong IP protection significantly increases investor confidence. InventraIP's commercialization services help identify licensing targets, market opportunities, and strategic partnerships.

Technology Landscape and
Whitespace Analysis

A graphical representation of the current state of a specific technology — revealing key players, trends, and untapped opportunities within a country, region, or globally.

Overview

Why Technology Landscape Analysis?

The basis for a global understanding of risks and opportunities within a given field of technology is patent and technological landscape analysis. They provide valuable business insights — revealing the most important players in a technological industry and what solutions they provide, based on available patent and scientific data.

Technology Landscape / Whitespace Analysis may be two types depending on business strategy:

Patent Landscapes

Provide a visual of all technology trends and owners based on patents for a given area of technology.

Technology Landscapes

Bring together all patents and technical articles for a given area of technology, revealing technology trends and owners.

Technology Watch

Monitoring of technology is critical to ensuring its market value. In today's technology-explosion world, keeping an eye on trends that could become threats — or opportunities — is essential.

Overview

Why Technology Watch?

Each year, companies and startups introduce hundreds of newer technologies. It's becoming increasingly hard — and equally important — to keep an eye on technology trends that can turn into threats and, if the right measures are taken, be converted into opportunities.

Key Business Reasons

  • ✓ Encourage R&D activities by keeping abreast of technological advancements
  • ✓ Access up-to-date information on relevant acquisitions

Services / Commercialization / Design Patent Search

Design Patent Search

Accurate Design Patent Drawings pledges to shield your IP. A design patent search involves looking through existing patents to ensure that your design hasn't been patented before.

Overview

Protect the Look and Feel of Your Product

For original, fresh, and ornamental designs for an item, a design patent is available. It is valid for 14 years from the date of filing. It also permits an innovator to come up with a novel technique to develop a product that already exists. The design patent protects this one-of-a-kind design without affecting the item's utility patent.

Who Needs Design Patent Search?

  • → Companies looking for better, novel designs
  • → Businesses in the process of creating or releasing a new product
  • → Parties who want to challenge a design's validity
  • → Companies checking if a new product design infringes existing prior art
  • → Consumer electronics, automotive, apparel, jewellery, and packaging industries

Our Search Expertise

Our search experts are well acquainted with combination strategies that produce relevant results — apt selection and combination of design patent classes, subclasses, and visual keywords.
